questions.label: Easy
body: An arithmetic sequence has first term 7 and common difference 4. Find its 18th term.
solution:
Use un = u1 + (n - 1)d.
u18 = 7 + (18 - 1)(4) = 75.

questions.label: Medium
body: An arithmetic sequence has first term -5 and common difference 6. Find its 14th term.
solution:
Use un = u1 + (n - 1)d.
u14 = -5 + (14 - 1)(6) = 73.

questions.label: Easy
body: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of the arithmetic sequence 3, 8, 13, ... .
solution:
The last term is 3 + 19(5) = 98.
S20 = 20/2 (3 + 98) = 1010.

questions.label: Medium
body: Find the sum of the first 16 terms of the arithmetic sequence 40, 38, 36, ... .
solution:
The last term is 40 + 15(-2) = 10.
S16 = 16/2 (40 + 10) = 400.

questions.label: Medium
body: Find the sum of the first 25 terms of the arithmetic sequence -7, -3, 1, ... .
solution:
The last term is -7 + 24(4) = 89.
S25 = 25/2 (-7 + 89) = 1025.

questions.label: Hard
body: Find the sum of the first 30 terms of the arithmetic sequence 1/2, 2, 7/2, ... .
solution:
The last term is 1/2 + 29(3/2) = 44.
S30 = 30/2 (1/2 + 44) = 1335/2.

solution:
un = u1rn-1.
u9 = (3)(2)8 = 768.

questions.label: Easy
body: Find the exact sum of the first 7 terms of a geometric series with first term 2 and common ratio 3.
solution:
Sn = a(1 - rn)/(1 - r).
S7 = 2(1 - (3)7)/(1 - (3)) = 2186.

questions.label: Medium

solution:
Sn = a(1 - rn)/(1 - r).
S6 = 96(1 - (1/2)6)/(1 - (1/2)) = 189.

questions.label: Medium
body: Find the exact sum of the first 8 terms of a geometric series with first term 5 and common ratio -2.
solution:
Sn = a(1 - rn)/(1 - r).
S8 = 5(1 - (-2)8)/(1 - (-2)) = -425.

questions.label: Easy
body: A quantity starts at 2000. It changes by 5% per year upwards. Find its value after 3 years, giving an exact value.
solution:
The multiplier is 1 + 1/20 = 21/20.
Value = 2000(21/20)3 = 9261/4.

questions.label: Medium
body: A quantity starts at 4800. It changes by 10% per year upwards. Find its value after 4 years, giving an exact value.
solution:
The multiplier is 1 + 1/10 = 11/10.
Value = 4800(11/10)4 = 175692/25.

questions.label: Medium
body: A quantity starts at 12000. It changes by 8% per year downwards. Find its value after 2 years, giving an exact value.
solution:
The multiplier is 1 - 2/25 = 23/25.
Value = 12000(23/25)2 = 50784/5.

questions.label: Hard
body: A quantity starts at 7500. It changes by 6% per year upwards. Find its value after 5 years, giving an exact value.
solution:
The multiplier is 1 + 3/50 = 53/50.
Value = 7500(53/50)5 = 1254586479/125000.

solution:
Write the right side with base 2: 82 = 26.
Equate exponents: 3x + 7 = 6. Hence x = -1/3.

questions.label: Easy
body: Solve log<sub>2</sub>(x - 3) = 5.
solution:
By the definition of a logarithm, x - 3 = (2)5.
Therefore x = 35. The logarithm argument is positive at this value.

questions.label: Medium
body: Solve log<sub>3</sub>(x + 4) = 3.
solution:
By the definition of a logarithm, x + 4 = (3)3.
Therefore x = 23. The logarithm argument is positive at this value.

questions.label: Easy
body: Find the coefficient of x<sup>3</sup> in the expansion of (1 + 2x)<sup>6</sup>.
solution:
The x3 term is C(6, 3)(2x)3.
Coefficient = C(6, 3)(2)3 = 20(8) = 160.

solution:
The x4 term is C(7, 4)(-1x)4.

questions.label: Medium
body: Find the coefficient of x<sup>2</sup> in the expansion of (1 + 3x)<sup>8</sup>.
solution:
The x2 term is C(8, 2)(3x)2.
Coefficient = C(8, 2)(3)2 = 28(9) = 252.

questions.label: Hard
body: Find the coefficient of x<sup>6</sup> in the expansion of (1 - 2x)<sup>10</sup>.
solution:
The x6 term is C(10, 6)(-2x)6.
Coefficient = C(10, 6)(-2)6 = 210(64) = 13440.

questions.label: Easy
body: Rationalize the denominator and simplify 1/(3 + 2√2).
solution:
Multiply by the conjugate (3 - 2√2).
1/(3 + 2√2) = (3 - 2√2)/(9 - 4·2) = (3 - 2√2)/1.

questions.label: Medium
body: Rationalize the denominator and simplify 1/(5 - 1√2).
solution:
Multiply by the conjugate (5 + 1√2).
1/(5 - 1√2) = (5 + 1√2)/(25 - 1·2) = (5 + 1√2)/23.

questions.label: Medium
body: Rationalize the denominator and simplify 1/(7 + 3√2).
solution:
Multiply by the conjugate (7 - 3√2).
1/(7 + 3√2) = (7 - 3√2)/(49 - 9·2) = (7 - 3√2)/31.

questions.label: Hard
body: Rationalize the denominator and simplify 1/(2 - 5√2).
solution:
Multiply by the conjugate (2 + 5√2).
1/(2 - 5√2) = (2 + 5√2)/(4 - 25·2) = (2 + 5√2)/-46.

body: Solve |x - 3| ≤ 5.
solution:
|x - 3| ≤ 5 means -5 ≤ x - 3 ≤ 5.
Adding 3 gives -2 ≤ x ≤ 8.

solution:

Adding -2 gives -6 ≤ x ≤ 2.

solution:
|x - 7| ≤ 3 means -3 ≤ x - 7 ≤ 3.
Adding 7 gives 4 ≤ x ≤ 10.

questions.label: Hard
solution:
|x - 1/2| ≤ 7/2 means -7/2 ≤ x - 1/2 ≤ 7/2.
Adding 1/2 gives -3 ≤ x ≤ 4.

questions.label: Easy
body: Given f(x) = 3x - 5, find f<sup>-1</sup>(x).
solution:
Let y = 3x - 5. Interchange x and y: x = 3y - 5.
So y = (x + 5)/3. Hence f-1(x) = (x + 5)/3.

questions.label: Medium
body: Given f(x) = -2x + 7, find f<sup>-1</sup>(x).
solution:
Let y = -2x + 7. Interchange x and y: x = -2y + 7.
So y = (x - 7)/-2. Hence f-1(x) = (x - 7)/-2.

questions.label: Medium
body: Given f(x) = 1/2x + 4, find f<sup>-1</sup>(x).
solution:
Let y = 1/2x + 4. Interchange x and y: x = 1/2y + 4.
So y = (x - 4)/1/2. Hence f-1(x) = (x - 4)/1/2.

questions.label: Hard
body: Given f(x) = 5x - 3/2, find f<sup>-1</sup>(x).
solution:
Let y = 5x - 3/2. Interchange x and y: x = 5y - 3/2.
So y = (x + 3/2)/5. Hence f-1(x) = (x + 3/2)/5.

questions.label: Easy
body: Let f(x) = (2x + 3)/(x + 1), x ≠ -1. Find f<sup>-1</sup>(x) and state its domain.
solution:
Set y = (2x + 3)/(x + 1). Then yx + 1y = 2x + 3, so x(y - 2) = 3 - 1y.
Therefore f-1(x) = (3 - 1x)/(x - 2), with domain x ≠ 2.

questions.label: Medium
body: Let f(x) = (4x - 1)/(x + 2), x ≠ -2. Find f<sup>-1</sup>(x) and state its domain.
solution:
Set y = (4x - 1)/(x + 2). Then yx + 2y = 4x - 1, so x(y - 4) = -1 - 2y.
Therefore f-1(x) = (-1 - 2x)/(x - 4), with domain x ≠ 4.

questions.label: Medium
body: Let f(x) = (-3x + 5)/(x - 2), x ≠ 2. Find f<sup>-1</sup>(x) and state its domain.
solution:
Set y = (-3x + 5)/(x - 2). Then yx + -2y = -3x + 5, so x(y - -3) = 5 - -2y.
Therefore f-1(x) = (5 - -2x)/(x - -3), with domain x ≠ -3.

questions.label: Hard
body: Let f(x) = (1x + 6)/(x + 4), x ≠ -4. Find f<sup>-1</sup>(x) and state its domain.
solution:
Set y = (1x + 6)/(x + 4). Then yx + 4y = 1x + 6, so x(y - 1) = 6 - 4y.
Therefore f-1(x) = (6 - 4x)/(x - 1), with domain x ≠ 1.

questions.label: Easy
body: The function is f(x) = 1(x - 3)<sup>2</sup> - 4. State the vertex, axis of symmetry and whether the vertex is a maximum or minimum.
solution:
This is vertex form a(x - h)2 + k.
Vertex: (3, -4); axis: x = 3. Since a is positive, the vertex is a minimum.

Vertex: (-1/2, 7/4); axis: x = -1/2. Since a is positive, the vertex is a minimum.

questions.label: Easy
body: The equation x<sup>2</sup> + 6x + k = 0 has exactly one real solution. Find k and the repeated root.
solution:
Exactly one real root requires Δ = b2 - 4ac = 0.
36 - 4k = 0, so k = 9.
The repeated root is x = -b/2a = -3.

questions.label: Medium
body: The equation x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + k = 0 has exactly one real solution. Find k and the repeated root.
solution:

16 - 4k = 0, so k = 4.
The repeated root is x = -b/2a = -2.

questions.label: Medium
body: The equation x<sup>2</sup> - 8x + k = 0 has exactly one real solution. Find k and the repeated root.

The repeated root is x = -b/2a = -5.

questions.label: Easy
body: The graph y = f(x) is transformed to y = 2f(x + 3) + 4. Describe the transformations, in a valid order.
solution: Start with y = f(x). Translate 3 units left. Then apply a vertical stretch by factor 2. Finally translate 4 units up.

questions.label: Medium
body: The graph y = f(x) is transformed to y = 1/2f(x - 2) - 5. Describe the transformations, in a valid order.
solution: Start with y = f(x). Translate 2 units right. Then apply a vertical stretch by factor 1/2. Finally translate 5 units down.

questions.label: Medium
body: The graph y = f(x) is transformed to y = -1f(x + 4) + 3. Describe the transformations, in a valid order.
solution: Start with y = f(x). Translate 4 units left. Then apply a reflection in the x-axis. Finally translate 3 units up.

questions.label: Hard
body: The graph y = f(x) is transformed to y = 3f(x - 1) - 2. Describe the transformations, in a valid order.
solution: Start with y = f(x). Translate 1 units right. Then apply a vertical stretch by factor 3. Finally translate 2 units down.

questions.label: Easy
body: For f(x) = (2x + 6)/(x - 3), state the vertical and horizontal asymptotes and find both axis intercepts.
solution:
The denominator is zero at x = 3, so this is the vertical asymptote. Equal polynomial degrees give horizontal asymptote y = 2.
x-intercept: 2x + 6 = 0, so x = -3.
y-intercept: f(0) = 6/-3 = -2.

questions.label: Medium
body: For f(x) = (-1x + 4)/(x + 2), state the vertical and horizontal asymptotes and find both axis intercepts.
solution:
The denominator is zero at x = -2, so this is the vertical asymptote. Equal polynomial degrees give horizontal asymptote y = -1.
x-intercept: -1x + 4 = 0, so x = 4.
y-intercept: f(0) = 4/2 = 2.

questions.label: Medium
body: For f(x) = (3x - 9)/(x + 1), state the vertical and horizontal asymptotes and find both axis intercepts.
solution:
The denominator is zero at x = -1, so this is the vertical asymptote. Equal polynomial degrees give horizontal asymptote y = 3.
x-intercept: 3x - 9 = 0, so x = 3.
y-intercept: f(0) = -9/1 = -9.

questions.label: Hard
body: For f(x) = (4x + 5)/(x - 2), state the vertical and horizontal asymptotes and find both axis intercepts.
solution:
The denominator is zero at x = 2, so this is the vertical asymptote. Equal polynomial degrees give horizontal asymptote y = 4.
x-intercept: 4x + 5 = 0, so x = -5/4.
y-intercept: f(0) = 5/-2 = -5/2.

questions.label: Easy
body: A model is P(t) = 80(2)<sup>t</sup>. Find P(5) exactly and state whether the model represents growth or decay.
solution:
P(5) = 80(2)5 = 2560.
Because the base 2 is greater than 1, the model represents growth.

questions.label: Medium
body: A model is P(t) = 640(1/2)<sup>t</sup>. Find P(4) exactly and state whether the model represents growth or decay.
solution:
P(4) = 640(1/2)4 = 40.
Because the base 1/2 is between 0 and 1, the model represents decay.

questions.label: Medium
body: A model is P(t) = 150(3)<sup>t</sup>. Find P(3) exactly and state whether the model represents growth or decay.
solution:
P(3) = 150(3)3 = 4050.
Because the base 3 is greater than 1, the model represents growth.

questions.label: Hard
body: A model is P(t) = 1000(4/5)<sup>t</sup>. Find P(6) exactly and state whether the model represents growth or decay.
solution:
P(6) = 1000(4/5)6 = 32768/125.
Because the base 4/5 is between 0 and 1, the model represents decay.

questions.label: Easy
body: Find the x-coordinates of the points where y = x<sup>2</sup> intersects y = 3x + 4.
solution:
At intersections, x2 = 3x + 4, so x2 - 3x - 4 = 0.
Solving gives x = 4 or x = -1.

solution:

Solving gives x = 2 or x = -3.

solution:
At intersections, x2 = 5x - 4, so x2 - 5x + 4 = 0.
Solving gives x = 4 or x = 1.

solution:

Solving gives x = 4 or x = -2.

questions.label: Easy
body: Solve |x - 2| - 1 = 5.
solution: |x - 2| = 6, so x - 2 = ±6. Hence x = 8 or x = -4.

questions.label: Medium
solution: |x + 3| = 6, so x + 3 = ±6. Hence x = 3 or x = -9.

solution: |x - 1| = -4. An absolute value cannot be negative, so there is no real solution.

questions.label: Easy
body: Points A(1, 2) and B(7, 10) are given. Find the midpoint of AB and the exact length AB.
solution:
Midpoint = ((1 + 7)/2, (2 + 10)/2) = (4, 6).
AB = √((6)2 + (8)2) = 10.

questions.label: Medium
body: Points A(-3, 5) and B(5, -1) are given. Find the midpoint of AB and the exact length AB.
solution:
Midpoint = ((-3 + 5)/2, (5 + -1)/2) = (1, 2).
AB = √((8)2 + (-6)2) = 10.

questions.label: Medium

solution:
Midpoint = ((2 + -4)/2, (-4 + 4)/2) = (-1, 0).
AB = √((-6)2 + (8)2) = 10.

questions.label: Easy
body: Find the equation of the line with gradient 3 passing through (2, 5). Give the answer in the form y = mx + c.
solution:
Use y - y1 = m(x - x1): y - (5) = 3(x - (2)).
Therefore y = 3x - 1.

questions.label: Medium
body: Find the equation of the line with gradient -2 passing through (-1, 4). Give the answer in the form y = mx + c.
solution:
Use y - y1 = m(x - x1): y - (4) = -2(x - (-1)).
Therefore y = -2x + 2.

questions.label: Medium
body: Find the equation of the line with gradient 1/2 passing through (6, -3). Give the answer in the form y = mx + c.
solution:
Use y - y1 = m(x - x1): y - (-3) = 1/2(x - (6)).
Therefore y = 1/2x - 6.

questions.label: Hard
body: Find the equation of the line with gradient -4/3 passing through (3/2, -2). Give the answer in the form y = mx + c.
solution:
Use y - y1 = m(x - x1): y - (-2) = -4/3(x - (3/2)).
Therefore y = -4/3x + 0.

questions.label: Easy
body: A line L has gradient 2. Find the equation of the line perpendicular to L that passes through (3, 1).
solution:
Perpendicular gradients multiply to -1, so the required gradient is -1/2.
Using point-gradient form gives y - (1) = -1/2(x - (3)), hence y = -1/2x + 5/2.

questions.label: Medium
body: A line L has gradient -3. Find the equation of the line perpendicular to L that passes through (-2, 4).
solution:
Perpendicular gradients multiply to -1, so the required gradient is 1/3.
Using point-gradient form gives y - (4) = 1/3(x - (-2)), hence y = 1/3x + 14/3.

questions.label: Medium
body: A line L has gradient 1/2. Find the equation of the line perpendicular to L that passes through (6, -5).
solution:
Perpendicular gradients multiply to -1, so the required gradient is -2.
Using point-gradient form gives y - (-5) = -2(x - (6)), hence y = -2x + 7.

questions.label: Hard
body: A line L has gradient -4/3. Find the equation of the line perpendicular to L that passes through (1/2, 2).
solution:
Perpendicular gradients multiply to -1, so the required gradient is 3/4.
Using point-gradient form gives y - (2) = 3/4(x - (1/2)), hence y = 3/4x + 13/8.

questions.label: Easy
body: A circle has centre (3, -2) and radius 5. Write its equation and determine whether the origin lies inside, on or outside the circle.
solution:
Equation: (x - 3)2 + (y + 2)2 = 25.
For the origin, distance squared from the centre is 13; r2 = 25. Therefore the origin lies inside the circle.

questions.label: Medium
body: A circle has centre (-4, 1) and radius 3. Write its equation and determine whether the origin lies inside, on or outside the circle.
solution:
Equation: (x + 4)2 + (y - 1)2 = 9.
For the origin, distance squared from the centre is 17; r2 = 9. Therefore the origin lies outside the circle.

questions.label: Medium
body: A circle has centre (0, 6) and radius 7. Write its equation and determine whether the origin lies inside, on or outside the circle.
solution:
Equation: (x + 0)2 + (y - 6)2 = 49.

body: A differentiable function satisfies f'(x) = 3(x + 2)(x - 2). Determine the intervals on which f is increasing and decreasing.
solution:
Critical values are x = -2 and x = 2. The derivative is positive outside the roots and negative between them.
Increasing on (-∞, -2) ∪ (2, ∞); decreasing on (-2, 2).

questions.label: Hard
body: A differentiable function satisfies f'(x) = 3(x - 1)(x - 4). Determine the intervals on which f is increasing and decreasing.
solution:
Critical values are x = 1 and x = 4. The derivative is positive outside the roots and negative between them.
Increasing on (-∞, 1) ∪ (4, ∞); decreasing on (1, 4).

questions.label: Easy
body: A rectangle has perimeter 40. Let one side be x. Express its area A in terms of x, then find the maximum possible area.
solution:
The other side is 20 - x, so A(x) = x(20 - x) = 20x - x2.
A'(x) = 20 - 2x = 0 gives x = 10. Since A''(x) = -2, this is a maximum.
Maximum area = 100 square units.

howTo: This bank is designed for deliberate Paper 1 practice rather than passive reading. Attempt each question on separate paper, without a calculator. Mark only after completing a set, then record the reason for every lost mark: concept, algebra, notation, interpretation or time pressure.

steps.text: Select one subtopic and attempt four consecutive questions.
Use roughly 1.1 minutes per mark on mixed sets.
Award method marks only when the required reasoning is visible.
Redo missed questions after 48 hours without viewing the solution.
